about: A reviewer's decisions over the generated truth, applied by name after the sources are merged: which statements of different parents describe one event, which source's instant stands where the automatic order would pick another, and notes a reader should see. Edit this file, never data/breakups.json.

overrides.name: ullage-motor-2009-070-december-2019
overrides.note: NASA puts the December 2019 breakup on 2009-070F (36116), GCAT on 2009-070E (36115): one event, the parent as NASA names it.

overrides.name: h-iia-2018-084-february-2019
overrides.note: NASA splits the 6 to 7 February 2019 H-IIA cloud over the PES upper cap (43675) and the second stage (43682, 'prior to Sept. 2019'); GCAT puts it on the second stage at 06:00. Merged as one event under the upper cap, which NASA dates.

overrides.name: meteor-2-7-2004
overrides.note: NASA lists Meteor 2-7's 2004 anomalous event in March 2004 and GCAT dates the cloud 'Jul?' 2004: one event, NASA's month standing.

overrides.name: briz-km-2015-2016
overrides.note: NASA lists the Briz-KM anomalous event on 29 April 2015 and GCAT dates the same cloud 'Jul?' 2016: one event, NASA's day standing.

overrides.name: cosmos-2535-2019-2020
overrides.note: NASA dates the Cosmos 2535 breakup 9 January 2020 at 22:00 GMT and GCAT '2019 Aug 3?': one event, NASA's instant standing, the five-month disagreement kept as a conflict.

overrides.name: iss-releases
overrides.exempt: objects released from the station on purpose, not a breakup
overrides.note: The catalogue lists what the station jettisons (tanks, tools, covers) as debris; a burst of them is a release, not a breakup.
